data.name: Adit
data.gender_notes: Adit is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: God of the Cosmos, the First God
data.long_meaning: Adit is the name of the first god in Hinduism, the god of the cosmos and the unlimited sky. He is also known as Aditya, the Sun God. Adit is the source of all creation, the infinite and the beginningless, and represents the pure consciousness. He is the deity of light and knowledge, and the embodiment of self-illumination.
data.etymology: Adit belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of the Cosmos, the First God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adit total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Adit is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and is widely recognized and revered in Hindu culture. Adit is considered as a significant celestial deity, and many temples and religious sites are dedicated to him in various parts of India. His influence is not only limited to India but has spread across various continents through Indian cultural diaspora.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu philosophy, Adit represents the pure, unbounded consciousness that transcends the physical world. He is a reminder of the infinite and eternal nature of the soul, urging us to seek self-realization and inner peace. Worshiping Adit is believed to bestow blessings of knowledge, wisdom, and self-illumination, which are essential for spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Adit is the name of the first god, the primal deity of the Rigveda, symbolizing the infinite, boundless, and endless cosmic light and consciousness, the origin of all creation.
